sourceFacts.fact: Most otitis media with effusion resolves without intervention, but persistent effusion beyond three months should trigger hearing assessment and ENT involvement.
Hearing difficulty matters even if speech development appears normal; management depends on the child's hearing and clinical context.

layoutSpecification: Title 'Persistent fluid: check hearing'. A long horizontal calendar strip begins LEFT with a symbolic blue drop labelled 'Effusion'. Teal time arrow runs to a highlighted calendar milestone at centre labelled 'Beyond 3 months'; no dates, no fictional patient data. From milestone a broad rightward arrow reaches a large pair of headphones on a plain stand labelled 'Hearing assessment', then a short arrow to an 'ENT review' appointment card. Below timeline a small speech bubble containing a simple star sits beside text 'Speech may still seem normal'. No audiogram, hearing threshold number, ear anatomy or automatic surgery arrow. This is persistent effusion follow-up, not a rule to wait when urgent clinical concerns exist.
